regulations_source: https://www.eregulations.com/assets/docs/resources/IN/26INFW_LR.pdf (2026-2027 Indiana Fishing Regulations Guide, the official regulations booklet linked from in.gov/dnr/fish-and-wildlife/fishing/fishing-guide-and-regulations/ -- Indiana DNR distributes its official regs text through eRegulations rather than hosting the PDF itself; the in.gov page carries a standard disclaimer that it doesn't endorse eRegulations' unrelated commercial content, but the regulations text itself is DNR's own)

regulations_summary.largemouth_bass: LAKES: 5/day, combined with smallmouth and spotted bass (any combination), 14 in minimum, statewide. RIVERS/STREAMS (different rule, confirmed 2026-08-20 -- the original research pass missed this distinction and only recorded the lakes number): 5/day combined, but a PROTECTED SLOT instead of a flat minimum -- 'no fish 12 to 15 inches may be kept, and no more than two fish over 15 inches may be kept.' Always ask/confirm whether the water in question is a lake or a river/stream before quoting a bass limit -- the two rules are materially different, not just a rounding difference.
regulations_summary.smallmouth_bass: Same LAKES vs RIVERS/STREAMS split as largemouth bass above (combined bag) -- see largemouth_bass entry for the exact wording.
regulations_summary.crappie_black_and_white: 25/day (black and white crappie combined), no statewide minimum size
regulations_summary.bluegill: unlimited daily bag, no minimum size, statewide
regulations_summary.common_carp: explicitly unregulated -- no bag limit, no size limit, no closed season; listed among invasive/rough species (with bowfin, buffalo, gar, shad, suckers) that may be taken year-round including by bow and spear; the only carp-specific rule found is that carp may not be used as live bait
regulations_summary.channel_catfish: 10/day in lakes, combined with blue and flathead catfish under one 10-fish aggregate bag; within that 10, no more than one channel catfish 28 in or longer may be kept
regulations_summary.blue_catfish: 10/day in lakes, combined with channel and flathead catfish under one 10-fish aggregate bag; within that 10, no more than one blue catfish 35 in or longer may be kept
regulations_summary.flathead_catfish: 10/day in lakes, combined with channel and blue catfish under one 10-fish aggregate bag; within that 10, no more than one flathead catfish 35 in or longer may be kept
regulations_summary.walleye: 6/day, combined with walleye-sauger hybrid and sauger (any combination); 14 in minimum south of SR 26, 16 in minimum north of SR 26
regulations_summary.northern_pike: 3/day, 24 in minimum, no more than one 30 in or longer
regulations_summary.muskellunge: 1/day (1 muskellunge OR 1 tiger muskellunge), 36 in minimum
regulations_summary.trout_combined: Indiana regulates trout as a COMBINED GROUP, not species by species. 5/day total in any combination of brook, rainbow and brown trout, of which NO MORE THAN 1 may be a brown trout. STREAMS: 7 in minimum size; season runs 6 a.m. local on the last Saturday in April through Dec 31; catch-and-release only Jan 1 - Apr 14; CLOSED Apr 15 until the last Saturday in April while DNR completes annual stocking (this closure applies to a named list of streams -- Pigeon River/Creek, Harding Run, Curtis Creek, Bloody Run, Graveyard Run, Turkey Creek, Mississinewa River in Randolph Co. WMA, Big Blue River in Wilbur Wright FWA -- not statewide). INLAND LAKES: no closed season and NO minimum size, except an 18 in minimum for BROWN TROUT specifically at Oliver, Olin and Martin lakes (LaGrange Co.) and the Brookville Lake tailwater / East Fork Whitewater River (Franklin Co.). This is a real lakes-vs-streams split, same pattern as the bass rule -- confirm which water type before quoting a limit.
regulations_summary.rainbow_trout: See trout_combined -- Indiana does not give rainbow trout a separate limit.
regulations_summary.brown_trout: See trout_combined. Brown trout is the one species carved out of the combined limit: max 1 of the 5-fish daily bag may be a brown trout, and it carries the only lake-specific 18 in minimum.
regulations_summary.brook_trout: See trout_combined -- Indiana does not give brook trout a separate limit.
regulations_summary.kokanee_salmon: NOT FOUND in Indiana's inland regulations -- kokanee is a coldwater reservoir species not known to be established here. Do not infer a limit; if a specific Indiana water is claimed to hold kokanee, verify directly with DNR rather than reading across from the trout rule.
water_specific_examples_found: Patoka Lake: largemouth bass 15 in minimum (overrides the 14 in statewide minimum)
Cecil M. Harden Lake: largemouth bass 16 in minimum (overrides the 14 in statewide minimum)

Fidler Pond (Elkhart County): largemouth bass 18 in minimum, 2 fish daily bag (vs. statewide 14 in / 5 fish); also a separate 15/day combined bluegill-redear-crappie limit and a 5/day channel catfish limit at this pond specifically
Turtle Creek Reservoir (Sullivan County): largemouth bass 20 in minimum, 1 fish daily bag

Sugar Creek (Montgomery/Parke/Boone/Clinton/Tipton counties): black bass 20 in minimum, 1 fish daily bag -- a WATER-SPECIFIC override, confirmed 2026-08-20 to NOT be the general statewide rivers/streams rule (see largemouth_bass entry above for that). The regs guide lists Sugar Creek under its own 'Special Regulations for Rivers & Streams' section specifically because it's an exception to the general river slot rule, not an example of it.

Little Elkhart River, Solomon Creek and Cobus Creek (Elkhart Co., 2.8 mi total) -- permanent catch-and-release, artificial lures or flies only, trout water. Year-round designation, not a seasonal closure.

closed_seasons.note: CORRECTED 2026-08-21 -- the original version of this note said trout was not a species this toolkit models and dismissed the trout closure as irrelevant. That is now wrong: trout was added to species.yaml and to regulations_summary above, so the closure below IS a live answer, not a footnote. NO CLOSED SEASON for the eleven warmwater/coolwater species (largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, crappie, bluegill, common carp, channel/blue/flathead catfish, walleye, northern pike, muskellunge) in lakes and reservoirs -- confirmed directly against the current 2026-2027 regs text, not assumed from prior research. This matches SKILL.md rule 4. TROUT IS THE EXCEPTION and DOES have closed-season rules: on designated inland trout STREAMS, catch-and-release only Jan 1 - Apr 14, then CLOSED Apr 15 until the last Saturday in April, reopening 6 a.m. that day through Dec 31 -- see the trout_combined entry in regulations_summary for the full detail and the named stream list. Inland LAKES have no trout closed season. Also noted: Lake Michigan smelt may only be taken Mar 1 - May 30, but smelt is not a modeled species and Lake Michigan is a separate regulatory layer either way (SKILL.md rule 7).

license_summary.resident_senior_65plus_1yr: $3.00 (residents born after March 31, 1943, i.e. age ~64+ per current wording)
license_summary.trout_salmon_stamp_privilege: $11.00, required in addition to a base license to keep trout/salmon
license_summary.license_year: Annual licenses run April 1 through March 31 of the following year
license_summary.source: Cross-checked against both the regulations PDF (regulations_source) and the official fee schedule at https://www.in.gov/dnr/fish-and-wildlife/licenses-and-permits/license-fees -- both agreed. Fees current for the 2026-2027 season as fetched 2026-08-20; confirm before relying on them past this season.
license_summary.where_to_buy: Online and via the free GoOutdoorsIN mobile app at gooutdoorsin.com (Indiana's official license portal, the 'Activity Hub' -- charges a $3 tech fee plus card processing on top of the licence price), and in person at authorized retailers (bait shops, sporting goods stores) and most DNR properties, findable through the portal's retailer locator. Verified 2026-08-21 against in.gov/dnr/fish-and-wildlife/licenses-and-permits/.

stocking_source: https://www.in.gov/dnr/fish-and-wildlife/fishing/indiana-fish-stocking/indiana-fish-stocking-dashboard -- an embedded Tableau Public Server dashboard (workbook 'FishStockingDatabase/PublicDashboard', hosted at datavizpublic.in.gov, Indiana's own public-facing Tableau server) with an interactive map and a filterable table (waterbody, year, species, amount stocked), described by DNR as updating every 24 hours. VERIFIED by direct fetch (not by trusting the referral page): curl against https://datavizpublic.in.gov/views/FishStockingDatabase/PublicDashboard returned HTTP 200 with the normal Tableau vizportal app shell and no redirect to a login/auth page -- unlike Ohio's data.ohio.gov stocking page, which explicitly demanded an account. This is a real point of difference between the two states' stocking data, not just a repeat of the same finding.
reciprocity: Confirms and extends SKILL.md rule 5. (1) Ohio River main stem: reciprocal between Indiana and Kentucky -- either state's license is valid on the main stem only, explicitly excluding embayments/tributaries, per the regs guide's own wording. (2) Calumet Harbor on Lake Michigan: reciprocal between Indiana and Illinois, harbor only, confirmed. (3) NEW FINDING not in the prior toolkit research: the Wabash River is also a reciprocal boundary water between Indiana and Illinois -- 'Officers of Illinois and Indiana will recognize and accept valid sport fishing licenses of either state when legally possessed and used on the Wabash River forming a common boundary between Illinois and Indiana' (quoted verbatim from the current regs guide). This should be added to SKILL.md rule 5's reciprocity list, not just this file, since it's a toolkit-wide fact, not an Indiana-only footnote.
great_lakes_note: Lake Michigan shoreline and tributaries in Indiana carry a separate regulatory layer not researched in depth here (per SKILL.md rule 7) -- confirmed to exist and to differ materially from inland rules (e.g. a 3-fish combined bass limit vs. 5 inland, a 15-fish yellow perch limit that doesn't exist inland, a smelt-only season March 1-May 30, and its own consumption-advisory categories), but the full Lake Michigan rule set was not catalogued. Treat any Lake Michigan-specific question as needing a direct check against the guide's Lake Michigan section, not this file's statewide/inland summary.
known_gaps: CORRECTED 2026-08-20 (second pass, live end-to-end test): the original research pass recorded only the lakes bass limit and missed that rivers/streams have a materially different protected-slot rule -- see largemouth_bass/smallmouth_bass entries above. Caught only because a real query (White River, a river) exposed the gap; worth treating as a reminder that 'in lakes' qualifiers anywhere in this file may hide an unrecorded rivers/streams counterpart -- don't assume a lakes number silently also covers rivers for any other species here either, it just hasn't been checked yet for walleye/pike/muskellunge/catfish/panfish/carp.
Water-specific overrides above are five examples, not an exhaustive list -- the regs guide has a longer special-regulations section not fully catalogued in this pass
